subject: Clearhaven DPA — subprocessor notice, successor obligations, and breach timelines
messages:
From: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@clearhaven.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@clearhaven.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial review: DPA redlines / subprocessor notice and breach timeline

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Procurement had a quick pass and flagged a few items we need clarified before we can route for legal sign-off:

- Subprocessor notice: the DPA currently says "prior notice" and allows 30 days. We need explicit language for emergency subprocessors and a firm minimum notice where possible. Can Redwood commit to 30 days for planned additions and 48 hours for emergency placements with follow-up details?
- Successor obligations: our procurement team needs a successor-vendor clause so that if Redwood transfers processing to a successor, Clearhaven’s rights and data protections carry over automatically.
- Breach notification timeline: we see a mix of 48/72-hour language. Procurement prefers a 72-hour preliminary notification window for any confirmed compromise, and a detailed final report within 15 business days. Do you have flexibility here?
- Execution: we use DocuSign for contracts. Your original note said AdobeSign is the standard. We can accept either, but procurement needs the envelope contact and an expected execution ETA.

I've attached our redlines (Redlined_DPA_v3.pdf) with inline comments. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Emily Sanders
Head of Procurement
Clearhaven Financial

Attachment: Redlined_DPA_v3.pdf (pdf, 182 KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial review: DPA redlines / subprocessor notice and breach timeline

Team — forwarding Clearhaven's procurement notes. Key asks summarized below and proposed position for negotiation:

1) Subprocessor notice
- Proposed Redwood position: 30 days' advance notice for scheduled subprocessors; for emergency subprocessors (e.g., failover, short-term CDN, incident response vendors) Redwood will notify within 48 hours of activation and provide the reason and security details within 5 business days.

2) Successor obligations
- We can accept a successor-obligations clause limited to assignments related to M&A or changes in control where the successor inherits Redwood's obligations, provided Redwood retains the right to engage subprocessors for specific technical operations. Suggest legal draft: "Any successor entity shall assume all obligations under this DPA with respect to Customer Data."

3) Breach timeline
- Proposed compromise: initial notification within 48 hours of confirming unauthorized access affecting personal data (informal short notice), followed by a substantive report within 10 business days containing forensics, scope, and remediation steps. For incidents under investigation where attribution is incomplete, we commit to an interim update within 72 hours and a full report within 15 business days.

4) Execution mechanics
- Redwood can accommodate DocuSign for this customer. We'll prepare a DocuSign envelope and share the link once redlines are resolved. Legal prefers to run final redline through our privacy counsel (Mina) before the envelope goes live.

Can you review and confirm you and legal are comfortable with the proposed compromise above? If so I will draft the negotiating language and share for review.

Thanks — Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@clearhaven.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial review: DPA redlines / subprocessor notice and breach timeline

Emily — thanks for the detailed notes and the redline. Quick note from the commercial side and a proposal to bridge procurement/legal concerns:

- Subprocessor notice: 30 days for planned additions; emergency placement notice within 48 hours plus a technical summary within 5 business days.
- Successor obligations: we can add a mutual assignment language so Clearhaven's protections transfer to a successor entity in a change of control; Redwood will ensure the successor adheres to the same DPA obligations.
- Breach timelines: to keep both sides comfortable, propose: initial notification within 48 hours if we have confirmed unauthorized access affecting personal data; if confirmation is pending, Redwood will send an interim update within 72 hours and a final report within 10 business days (or a rolling update plan if complex).

Attached is a simple mutual action plan (MAP_Clearhaven_v1.docx) that lays out milestones: legal sign-off, DocuSign envelope, procurement approval, and expected execution within 7 business days once redlines are agreed.

Next steps: if Clearhaven confirms the proposed compromise, Rishi's team will have Legal (Mina) insert the final language and we'll issue a DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP_Clearhaven_v1.docx (docx, 46 KB)
From: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@clearhaven.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@clearhaven.com
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial review: DPA redlines / subprocessor notice and breach timeline

Marissa / Rishi — appreciate the quick turnaround and pragmatic compromise. A few clarifying points from legal/procurement:

- Subprocessor list: procurement requires the current subprocessor list at signature and a monthly public registry. Can you provide the list as a CSV?
- Successor obligations: legal will want a short survivability clause and confirmation that data subject rights remain enforceable against the successor.
- Breach timeline: procurement still prefers 72 hours for preliminary notice, but given your 48/72 compromise, we can accept initial notification within 48 hours if the incident is confirmed; otherwise interim update within 72 hours. Final report: 15 business days maximum for high-severity incidents.
- Execution: DocuSign is preferred. Please share the envelope link and the signer contact for the procurement team. We will escalate to our GC if there are any remaining redlines.

We can sign-off on commercial terms quickly if you can supply: (1) CSV of current subprocessor list, (2) updated DPA with successor clause language, (3) DocuSign envelope link.

Thanks — Emily
Procurement, Clearhaven Financial
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@clearhaven.com>, procurement@clearhaven.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Initial review: DPA redlines / subprocessor notice and breach timeline

Emily / procurement — thanks, and good to have alignment. Per your checklist below, please find next artifacts and our firm commitments:

1) Subprocessor list: attached CSV (Subprocessor_List_2026-09-30.csv). This reflects current subprocessors and categories (analytics, hosting, monitoring, support). We will publish a monthly registry link post-signature.

2) Successor obligations language: inserted into the attached final redline (Final_DPA_Redline_for_Signing.pdf). Key snippet we propose: "In the event of a change of control or assignment that results in a successor entity, such successor shall assume all obligations under this Agreement and DPA with respect to Customer Data; such assignment shall not relieve Redwood of its liabilities for acts or omissions occurring prior to the assignment."

3) Breach notification and reporting: Redwood commits to the following:
   - Initial notification: within 48 hours of confirming unauthorized access affecting Clearhaven personal data.
   - Interim update: if confirmation is pending, Redwood will provide an interim update within 72 hours describing status and next investigative steps.
   - Substantive report: full incident report with scope, impact, and remediation plan within 10 business days for most incidents; for complex investigations Redwood will provide a rolling remediation timeline but will not exceed 15 business days for the substantive report without mutual agreement.
   - Cooperation: Redwood will provide reasonable cooperation, access to relevant logs/forensics, and a primary technical contact (security-incident@redwood.com).

4) Execution: We prepared a DocuSign envelope and set procurement@clearhaven.com as a signer; envelope link: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/EXAMPLE-ENVELOPE-ID-12345. Expect an email from DocuSign with an instruction and signer order.

If procurement confirms they will accept the Final_DPA_Redline_for_Signing.pdf and the CSV, we'll go live with the envelope today. Otherwise please list any final redlines and we will route to Mina for counsel review.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Final_DPA_Redline_for_Signing.pdf (pdf, 210 KB); Subprocessor_List_2026-09-30.csv (csv, 12 KB)
